questions.question: Where do you primarily expect to use the AI DJ?
options: Both private listening and live DJ sessions
Private listening and parties at home
Live gigs with an audience

questions.question: What kind of music will a typical playlist contain?
options: Related genres with some tempo variation
Mostly one genre and similar tempos
A wide mix of genres, eras and tempos

questions.interpretation: Support open-format playlists across genres, tempos and eras. Use BPM, harmonic compatibility and lyrical/vocal matching in selection and transitions. Exact lyrical matching behavior and data source remain to be clarified.

questions.question: How many songs should a typical playlist contain?
options: 15–50 songs
5–15 songs
50–150 songs
More than 150 songs

Under 1 hour
3–6 hours
More than 6 hours

questions.question: When you say the AI should play every song, how much of each song should it play?

The entire song, allowing overlap
Shorter DJ edits are fine if each song gets a meaningful section

questions.interpretation: AI selects musically appropriate portions of tracks. Set duration supports automatic AI selection, a user-defined time limit, or a user-defined duration range. Fit section and transition choices to these constraints while accounting for every playlist entry; handling infeasible combinations remains for R1-Q12.
presented_options: Most of the song, overlapping intros and outros
The entire song, allowing overlap
Shorter sections are fine, as long as each song gets a meaningful moment
Let me choose per set—full songs or a shorter DJ mix

questions.question: What mixing style should the AI use by default?

A balance of smooth mixing and creative performance
Active performance with loops, cuts and effects

questions.selected_option: AI chooses based on the music, with an option for me to select a style

A balance of smooth mixing and creative performance
Active performance with loops, cuts and effects
AI chooses based on the music, with an option for me to select a style

questions.question: How much should the AI alter a song’s tempo to make a transition work?

Allow moderate changes when the result sounds natural
Allow noticeable changes for a more creative mix

Moderate changes, provided the song still sounds natural
Noticeable changes are fine for creative mixing
AI decides within tempo limits I can configure

questions.question: How should the AI choose the energy flow of a set?

Infer the flow from the playlist automatically
Let me specify an energy curve across the set

Let me choose a preset, such as build-up, steady or chill

Automatic by default, with both presets and a custom curve available

questions.question: After choosing a playlist in AI Only mode, what should happen before music starts?

Prepare and start automatically, with the plan visible
Let me choose between review-first and automatic start

presented_options: Show the proposed set and wait for me to press Start
Prepare and start automatically, with the plan visible
Let me choose between review-first and automatic start

questions.question: How should opening and closing tracks be chosen?
options: AI chooses unless I pin an opener or closer
I always choose both
AI always chooses
questions.answer: If the question has an asnwer that is both AI choseable and user defined alwasy pick that

questions.question: Once a set starts, how freely may AI reorder the remaining songs?
options: Adapt the remaining order while respecting my pins
Keep the approved order unless I request a change
Adapt later songs but keep the next few committed
questions.answer: If the question has an asnwer that is both AI choseable and user defined alwasy pick that

questions.question: If a requested set duration is too short to include every song properly, what should happen?
options: Extend the duration to include every song
Ask whether to use shorter song sections
Ask me which songs to remove

presented_options: Include every song; extend the duration
Keep the time limit; ask me which songs to remove
Keep the time limit; AI selects a subset and shows the omissions
Flag the conflict and let me choose before starting

questions.question: If the same track appears twice in the supplied playlist, how should we handle it?
options: Keep both occurrences as intentional
Flag repeats before starting and let me confirm them
Ask me whether to keep each repeat when planning

questions.interpretation: Keep repeated playlist occurrences and show a non-blocking duplicate notice. Prefer musically suitable sections not previously played, using playback-section history; this is best effort rather than an absolute ban on repeated sections. Whether history should extend beyond the current session remains to be clarified.
presented_options: Keep every occurrence as intentional
Flag duplicates before starting and let me decide
Remove duplicates automatically

questions.question: If some playlist tracks are missing or cannot be played, what should happen before starting?
options: Show the issues and let me explicitly resolve or skip them
Block starting until every track is available
Offer a clearly labeled partial set for me to approve

questions.interpretation: Automatically skip missing/unreadable/unplayable entries and advance to the next playable song. Apply to preflight and confirmed load failures during the set. Preserve skipped occurrence and reason in history; do not mark it played or silently delete it from the source playlist. If no playable entries remain, end/report the condition rather than retrying indefinitely.
presented_options: Show the issues and let me resolve them or approve skips
Block starting until every track is available
Skip unavailable tracks automatically and clearly list what was skipped

questions.question: May the AI introduce songs that were not in the supplied playlist?
options: Only when I explicitly add or request them
It may suggest additions, but needs my approval
Never; use only the supplied playlist
questions.answer: C; or both. Like an option to mixx the list only or go free
questions.selected_option: User-selectable music pool: supplied playlist only or free Mixxx-library selection
questions.interpretation: Provide a per-set music-pool setting: restrict AI selection to the supplied playlist, or allow free selection/additions from the local Mixxx library. Keep this independent of AI Only, B2B and Playlist Only performance modes. Original occurrence accounting and selected duration policy still apply. Default music-pool choice is not specified.
presented_options: None—use only the supplied playlist
It may suggest additional tracks, but needs my approval
It may freely select additional tracks from my Mixxx library

questions.question: If you edit the original playlist in Mixxx while our set is running, how should the app respond?

Keep the starting snapshot until I manually refresh
Automatically update unplayed entries while preserving the active transition

Record source/plan revisions and edits in session history. Default setting is not specified.
presented_options: Automatically update the remaining set, preserving the active transition
Show the changes and ask whether to apply them
Keep the starting playlist until I manually refresh it
questions.later_resolution: Delegated R3-Q14 supplies the default source sync setting.

questions.question: Where should an arranged set be saved?
options: In our app, with an option to save a new Mixxx playlist
Automatically as a new Mixxx playlist and in our app
Only in our app unless I explicitly export it

questions.interpretation: Always support saving the arranged set in the app. Provide selectable behaviors: optionally save a new Mixxx playlist on request; automatically save a new Mixxx playlist as well; or keep the set in the app with manual file export. Preserve the original playlist. Default save behavior is not specified.
presented_options: In our app, with an option to save a new Mixxx playlist
Automatically in our app and as a new Mixxx playlist
In our app only, with manual file export available
questions.later_resolution: Delegated R3-Q14 supplies the default save setting.

questions.question: How should track preparation work before a set?
options: Prepare the whole playlist before performance starts
Prepare the first few tracks, then process ahead in the background
Use existing analysis immediately and prepare only missing information
questions.answer: option to override as well; for 18 d

Offer a prepare-everything-first setting and user overrides. The exact scope of overrides beyond preparation strategy (such as forced reanalysis or manual feature edits) remains to be specified.
presented_options: Prepare the entire playlist before playback starts
Prepare the first few tracks, then analyze ahead while playing
Reuse existing analysis and process only missing information
Combine B and C, with an optional prepare everything first setting

questions.question: How should the AI learn your musical preferences over time?
options: Save my explicit ratings and preferences locally
Also learn from my set edits and manual interventions
Keep each session independent unless I save a preset

options: Consistently smooth, natural transitions

rounds.topic: Modes, physical controllers and B2B handover

questions.question: Which physical MIDI controller will we use for the first real B2B test?
options: I already own one—I will give the brand and model
I own several—I will list them and choose a primary one
I do not have one yet; start with mouse/keyboard testing and validate hardware later
questions.answer: I have basic one liek hercules, reloop buddy
questions.interpretation: User has a basic MIDI controller and mentions Hercules and Reloop Buddy. Reloop Buddy is a named candidate; exact Hercules model, complete device inventory and primary test controller remain unconfirmed. No Mixxx compatibility is yet verified.

questions.question: Which performance mode should be selected when the app opens, with performance automation still disarmed?
options: AI Only
B2B
Playlist Only
Remember my last selected mode
questions.answer: d
questions.selected_option: Remember my last selected mode
questions.interpretation: Persist the last selected performance mode across app launches. Do not persist armed state or replay old actions. First-launch mode was not specified in this answer; delegated R2-Q20 later selects B2B disarmed.

questions.question: In B2B, what default quiet period should follow the last gesture before AI becomes eligible to retake a released control? The setting remains user-configurable.
options: About 1 second
About 3 seconds
About 5 seconds
questions.answer: 3 default sound ok; but like if the user turns down the bass or affect the AI should not take it over during that transition only next transition Ai should re control that item in B2B
questions.selected_option: 3 seconds, plus a hold for the rest of the current transition
questions.interpretation: Default configurable quiet period is 3 seconds. In B2B a manual adjustment owns that item for the rest of the current transition. AI cannot reclaim merely because the timer expires; reclaim is allowed at a later transition start only after input/touch release, quiet expiry and fresh reconciliation. If still touched or not quiet at that start, retain the hold. Start any new action from the actual user value.

questions.question: In AI Only, when should AI restore its plan after an ordinary manual knob adjustment?
options: Promptly, using a smooth adjustment
At the next suitable beat or bar
At the next transition
questions.answer: a
questions.selected_option: Promptly, using a smooth adjustment
questions.interpretation: In armed AI Only mode, respond promptly to ordinary manual knob adjustments with smooth, bounded recovery to the valid AI plan. No B2B hold or wait for the next transition. Global disarm, fresh-state checks and other execution guards still apply.

questions.question: Where should quick Disarm AI controls be available?
options: On-screen button only
On-screen button and keyboard shortcut
On-screen button, keyboard shortcut and assignable MIDI-controller button
questions.answer: c
questions.selected_option: On-screen button, keyboard shortcut and assignable MIDI-controller button
questions.interpretation: Provide a persistent on-screen Disarm AI button, a keyboard shortcut and an assignable physical MIDI-controller button. All reach deterministic disarm handling without waiting for the planner, apply in every mode, and leave current music playing. Record their input source and outcome in session history.

questions.question: When switching between AI Only and B2B during playback, should AI continue under the new mode or wait for another resume action?
options: Continue under the new mode after cancelling stale actions and reconciling state
Disarm and wait for me to press Resume AI
Ask me whether to continue each time
questions.answer: a
questions.selected_option: Continue under the new mode after cancelling stale actions and reconciling state
questions.interpretation: When already armed, switching between AI Only and B2B continues automatically under the new mode after old-mode action cancellation and current-state reconciliation. Preserve explicit disarm: a mode switch cannot arm a disarmed service. Playlist Only still disables AI performance output; its return-to-performance behavior remains to be specified.
questions.later_resolution: R2-Q07 resolves the return from Playlist Only.

questions.question: When returning from Playlist Only to AI Only or B2B while music is playing, how should AI performance begin?
options: Require me to press Start or Resume AI
Treat selecting the performance mode as permission to begin after checking current state
Ask whether to begin each time
questions.answer: b
questions.selected_option: Treat selecting the performance mode as permission to begin after checking current state
questions.interpretation: Switching from Playlist Only to AI Only or B2B is an explicit request to begin AI performance after stale-action cancellation and current-state reconciliation; no extra Start/Resume is needed for the mode transition itself. Distinguish mode-based suspension from an explicit Disarm AI latch, which remains until deliberately resumed. Never replay historical or old-mode commands.

questions.question: In B2B, if you manually load a different song in place of the AI queued song, what should happen to the original queued song?
options: Keep it available to play later in the set
Skip it for this set and record the replacement
Ask me whether to keep it or skip it
questions.answer: Ai should respect the new song, and adjust based on it
questions.interpretation: In B2B, accept the human-selected replacement track as the new musical direction. Cancel affected actions for the previous track, confirm the newly loaded identity and current state, and adapt the transition and remaining set around it while respecting human control holds. Do not restore the AI's old track choice or mark the displaced occurrence played. The answer does not specify whether the displaced occurrence should be requeued or skipped; keep its outcome unresolved rather than silently deciding.
questions.later_resolution: Delegated R2-Q10 retains displaced occurrences unless explicitly skipped.

questions.question: In B2B, if you press Pause or Stop on a deck, how should the AI respond?
options: Keep that deck paused until I resume it; AI can continue on the other deck
Suspend AI performance on all decks until I resume AI
Allow AI to restart that deck at the next suitable transition
questions.answer: Keep that deck paused until I resume it; AI can continue on the other deck
questions.selected_option: Keep that deck paused until I resume it; AI can continue on the other deck
questions.interpretation: Treat manual Pause/Stop as a latched transport hold on that deck. Cancel dependent transition actions; do not automatically play, cue-trigger or replace its track. Other independent work can continue. Human playback or explicit release of that deck hold permits fresh reconciliation; the ordinary 3-second timer cannot clear it.

questions.question: What happens to the unplayed song displaced by a manual replacement?
options: Keep it in the remaining set unless I explicitly skip it
Automatically skip it
Ask after every replacement
questions.answer: Keep it in the remaining set unless I explicitly skip it
questions.selected_option: Keep it in the remaining set unless I explicitly skip it
questions.interpretation: Preserve the displaced occurrence in the remaining set, reorder around the human choice and record the replacement. Never reload it immediately over the chosen song. If it already played partly, preserve its actual spans and interrupted status; completion follows meaningful-playback rules. An explicit user skip resolves it without falsely marking it played.

questions.question: How long can I reserve controls for myself in B2B?
options: Automatic transition holds plus optional control or deck pins until I release them
Only automatic holds
Disarm the whole AI for every manual hold
questions.answer: Automatic transition holds plus optional control or deck pins until I release them
questions.selected_option: Automatic transition holds plus optional control or deck pins until I release them
questions.interpretation: Provide per-control and per-deck manual pins in addition to routine transition holds. Pins remain until explicitly released; global Disarm remains separate. Releasing a pin permits reconciliation and the next eligible transition, not an abrupt value reset.

questions.question: How should AI infer interaction on a controller without touch sensors?
options: Use MIDI activity and observed changes, showing inferred inactivity
Require touch-capable hardware
Disable B2B on ordinary controllers
questions.answer: Use MIDI activity and observed changes, showing inferred inactivity
questions.selected_option: Use MIDI activity and observed changes, showing inferred inactivity
questions.interpretation: Use raw intent where available, including repeated identical values; otherwise use observed changes with uncertain origin. Show inferred inactivity rather than claiming physical touch detection. Apply the confirmed 3-second quiet and later-transition rules; uncertain manual divergence yields conservatively.

questions.question: How should physical knobs catch up after AI changes their software values?
options: Preserve Mixxx mapping and soft takeover where supported
Force immediate jumps to hardware positions
Rewrite every controller mapping
questions.answer: Preserve Mixxx mapping and soft takeover where supported
questions.selected_option: Preserve Mixxx mapping and soft takeover where supported
questions.interpretation: Preserve existing mapping behavior and verify pickup for each fixture. Offer supported soft takeover configuration with a clear mismatch indicator. Do not assume every controller supports pickup or motor feedback; do not reroute hardware through the AI service.

questions.question: May AI create or change cue points?
options: Use existing cues and keep AI suggestions separate unless I save them
Freely overwrite user cues
Never propose new cues
questions.answer: Use existing cues and keep AI suggestions separate unless I save them
questions.selected_option: Use existing cues and keep AI suggestions separate unless I save them
questions.interpretation: Read user cue/hotcue/intro-outro data and preserve it. Store AI entry/exit suggestions in the app; explicit Save cues can write supported markers through a verified host operation with conflict handling. Triggering a hotcue is distinct from editing its stored position.

questions.question: How should B2B handle manual jogging, scratching, seeking and loops?
options: Yield affected transport and replan around the resulting position
Let AI immediately restore its old playhead
Suspend every deck for every gesture
questions.answer: Yield affected transport and replan around the resulting position
questions.selected_option: Yield affected transport and replan around the resulting position
questions.interpretation: Cancel stale track/position actions, yield the affected transport and dependent transition steps, and use fresh beat/playhead/loop state afterward. Touch release and later-transition eligibility still apply; no snapback to the abandoned position. Independent work may continue.

questions.question: May I manually introduce a song outside a playlist-restricted set?
options: Yes; respect it and record it as a manual addition
Reject it
Switch the entire set to free selection automatically
questions.answer: Yes; respect it and record it as a manual addition
questions.selected_option: Yes; respect it and record it as a manual addition
questions.interpretation: Music-pool restrictions constrain AI selection. A human load is respected in B2B and recorded with manual provenance, without silently enabling free AI selection or deleting original required occurrences. Recheck duration and pins after the change.

questions.question: What should AI Only do after a manual track load?
options: Reconcile and recover a valid plan without abruptly replacing audible music
Always reload its old choice immediately
Switch automatically to B2B
questions.answer: Reconcile and recover a valid plan without abruptly replacing audible music
questions.selected_option: Reconcile and recover a valid plan without abruptly replacing audible music
questions.interpretation: AI remains authoritative in AI Only, but stale commands and active-deck replacement guards still apply. Observe the new identity/state, then choose a bounded recovery from the actual musical situation. Ordinary knobs recover promptly; manual loads never authorize blindly replaying old loads.

questions.question: What should happen when AI planning is late or fails?
options: Use a validated deterministic fallback when current state permits
Always stop mixing immediately
Replay the previous plan
questions.answer: Use a validated deterministic fallback when current state permits
questions.selected_option: Use a validated deterministic fallback when current state permits
questions.interpretation: A planner timeout can fall back to constrained ordering and a conservative prepared transition if state, analysis, capabilities and authority are fresh. Clearly label fallback. Otherwise preserve current audio, stop starting new transitions and show action needed. Never invent a late plan or blindly loop/replay actions.

questions.question: What should happen if MIDI feedback or the host connection is lost?
options: Disarm performance and require fresh state plus deliberate resume
Reconnect and replay queued actions
Continue sending from the last known state
questions.answer: Disarm performance and require fresh state plus deliberate resume
questions.selected_option: Disarm performance and require fresh state plus deliberate resume
questions.interpretation: Loss of trustworthy host feedback disarms new performance output. Cancel queues, release AI-owned momentary controls through a verified watchdog path, and preserve current playback where possible. Reconnection requires negotiation, fresh snapshots and deliberate rearm. A physical-controller disconnect alone yields/cancels uncertain affected B2B work and alerts; do not automatically grab its held controls.

questions.question: What should the initial mode and controller setup be?
options: B2B disarmed; guided selection of the actual controller
AI Only armed on launch
Assume a fixed Hercules model
questions.answer: B2B disarmed; guided selection of the actual controller
questions.selected_option: B2B disarmed; guided selection of the actual controller
questions.interpretation: First launch selects B2B disarmed; later launches remember the selected mode but remain disarmed. Use Reloop Buddy as a candidate, not a verified device. Setup must identify the actual attached model, mapping and ports; the unspecified Hercules model remains an evidence prerequisite, not a question blocking this plan.

rounds.topic: Session UI/history, operational limits and acceptance

questions.question: What should the main live session screen emphasize?
options: Layered tracks, AI intention, actual actions and human ownership
Raw MIDI bytes first
Only the next song
questions.answer: Layered tracks, AI intention, actual actions and human ownership
questions.selected_option: Layered tracks, AI intention, actual actions and human ownership
questions.interpretation: Show deck/track lanes, overlap, playhead, section boundaries, parameter curves and concise AI reasons. Label planned, sent, observed and uncertain states separately. Keep mode and Disarm visible. Raw bytes and causal/device details are available in an inspector.

questions.question: When should MIDI session recording run?
options: Automatically for each session, with visible status and pause controls
Only when manually started
Record AI messages only
questions.answer: Automatically for each session, with visible status and pause controls
questions.selected_option: Automatically for each session, with visible status and pause controls
questions.interpretation: Record raw AI output, physical input, host feedback, semantic events, intentions and outcomes by default whenever the app session is active. Continue across mode changes and disarm. Pausing capture creates an explicit gap; resume begins with a fresh snapshot. Include unknown/unmapped events, never mislabel them as AI or human.

questions.question: Should sessions record audio as well as MIDI data?
options: Data by default; optional explicit master-output recording
Always record audio and microphone
Never attach audio
questions.answer: Data by default; optional explicit master-output recording
questions.selected_option: Data by default; optional explicit master-output recording
questions.interpretation: Master-output audio capture is opt-in and separate from MIDI history. No microphone capture or broadcasting by default. The UI can attach an existing local recording and disclose alignment uncertainty. Record/broadcast capability exists in the coverage target but requires explicit operator intent.

questions.question: How should track waveforms appear?
options: Use prepared local waveforms when available, with clear placeholders
Invent a waveform from MIDI
Block the session until all waveforms finish
questions.answer: Use prepared local waveforms when available, with clear placeholders
questions.selected_option: Use prepared local waveforms when available, with clear placeholders
questions.interpretation: Generate or read verified local waveform assets outside MIDI handling; cache by file fingerprint. Show a timeline with duration/position while unavailable. Never present decorative or synthesized bars as measured audio. Audio playback in history, if enabled, remains isolated from performance MIDI.

questions.question: How should long sessions be stored and rendered?
options: Chunked journal and snapshots with bounded UI queries
Keep every event in browser memory
Discard raw data after drawing it
questions.answer: Chunked journal and snapshots with bounded UI queries
questions.selected_option: Chunked journal and snapshots with bounded UI queries
questions.interpretation: Use recoverable journal chunks and indexed snapshots; stream versioned JSON export. Propose 16 MiB chunks, snapshots at most 5 seconds apart, 1,000-event query pages and a separately bounded recorder queue. These are tunable design budgets, to be validated under dense jog/14-bit traffic. Raw capture is retained; only visual curves are downsampled.

questions.question: What initial session size should we validate?
options: Up to 6 hours and 250 playlist occurrences, with visible larger-set limits
Only 10-minute sets
Claim unlimited sessions
questions.answer: Up to 6 hours and 250 playlist occurrences, with visible larger-set limits
questions.selected_option: Up to 6 hours and 250 playlist occurrences, with visible larger-set limits
questions.interpretation: Initial acceptance envelope: 1 to 250 occurrences, roughly 10 minutes through 6 hours, including duplicates and open-format material. These are proposed test targets, not measured capacity or permanent product limits. Larger inputs must receive a visible capacity/preparation assessment without silent truncation. Full-feature inventory is not limited to two decks just because the first proof is.

questions.question: How should history retention work?
options: Keep until deleted; optional configurable automatic cleanup
Automatically delete after each session
Upload it all to a cloud service
questions.answer: Keep until deleted; optional configurable automatic cleanup
questions.selected_option: Keep until deleted; optional configurable automatic cleanup
questions.interpretation: Keep local history until deletion by default. Offer opt-in age/size cleanup, pinned sessions excluded. Show usage and low-disk warnings; propose warning at 5 GiB free and stop optional audio before data becomes endangered. Disk-full must preserve MIDI responsiveness and mark capture gaps, never silently erase sessions.

questions.question: How should sharing and export handle local files?
options: Versioned JSON with optional assets and a redacted sharing export
Always embed every audio file
Include absolute local paths in every shared file
questions.answer: Versioned JSON with optional assets and a redacted sharing export
questions.selected_option: Versioned JSON with optional assets and a redacted sharing export
questions.interpretation: Default local export includes event/schema/profile versions and stable track/occurrence references. Sharing mode removes unnecessary absolute paths and device identifiers; audio/waveform assets are opt-in with explicit relative references. Import validates sizes, versions and path traversal, remains read-only, and never sends MIDI.

questions.question: How can I correct what AI learns?
options: Ratings, notes, explainable preferences and reset controls
Let learning run invisibly
Require rating every transition
questions.answer: Ratings, notes, explainable preferences and reset controls
questions.selected_option: Ratings, notes, explainable preferences and reset controls
questions.interpretation: Support optional timestamped notes and transition/set ratings, inspectable learned preferences with evidence, edit/delete/reset and a disable-learning switch. Never treat every B2B gesture as a permanent preference. Learning is local and contextual; user-specified settings and pins win.

questions.question: How far back should repetition and preference learning look?
options: Current session strongly; optional recent history with controls
Current session only forever
Use all history equally
questions.answer: Current session strongly; optional recent history with controls
questions.selected_option: Current session strongly; optional recent history with controls
questions.interpretation: Default repetition checks prioritize the current session, with recent local history (30 days, configurable/off) as a soft signal. Prefer unplayed sections where musically useful; do not ban repeated material. Display/reset evidence and keep event archives separate from the preference model.

questions.question: What should matching lyrics mean musically?
options: Matching hooks or phrases first; themes as a weaker optional signal
Always overlap vocals with similar words
Ignore lyrics
questions.answer: Matching hooks or phrases first; themes as a weaker optional signal
questions.selected_option: Matching hooks or phrases first; themes as a weaker optional signal
questions.interpretation: Use confident repeated hooks, words or phrases for potential handoffs; themes and language are weaker optional selection signals. Respect phrase timing, BPM, harmony and vocal density. Never force a lyrical match that creates clashes; allow user emphasis, language and disable controls.

questions.question: Where should lyrical information come from initially?
options: Local metadata and supplied timed lyrics, with optional local transcription
Require an online lyrics service
Treat MIDI as the lyric source
questions.answer: Local metadata and supplied timed lyrics, with optional local transcription
questions.selected_option: Local metadata and supplied timed lyrics, with optional local transcription
questions.interpretation: Use available local tags/sidecar timed lyrics and optional local transcription in a separate analysis process. Preserve source, confidence and timing; no mandatory cloud service or automatic online lyric collection. Missing lyrics reduces that score, never makes a track unplayable. Select/benchmark actual tools during implementation, not by invented capability.

questions.question: What initial tempo-change limits should AI use?
options: Prefer within 3 percent, normally cap at 6 percent, user configurable
Allow unrestricted changes
Never change tempo
questions.answer: Prefer within 3 percent, normally cap at 6 percent, user configurable
questions.selected_option: Prefer within 3 percent, normally cap at 6 percent, user configurable
questions.interpretation: Propose absolute tempo offsets within 3% as preferred and 6% as the normal cap, configurable per set/track and distinguishable from half/double-time analysis. Use a different transition when limits conflict; evaluate pitch/key-lock effects by listening. Numeric values are assistant defaults, not user-specified musical laws.

questions.question: Which defaults should apply to a newly created set?
options: Playlist pool, source snapshot, review first, local autosave
Free library, live sync and automatic playback
Ask every setting before every set
questions.answer: Playlist pool, source snapshot, review first, local autosave
questions.selected_option: Playlist pool, source snapshot, review first, local autosave
questions.interpretation: Default to supplied-playlist pool, source snapshot until refresh, review-first start and local autosave with optional new Mixxx playlist. Retain all requested alternatives: free library selection, live source sync, automatic start for an explicitly initiated set, automatic dual save or local-only/manual export. Keep these independent of performance mode.

questions.question: How much musical planning can I override?
options: AI choices plus editable style, energy, duration, pins and section constraints
Only choose songs
Require hand-editing every transition
questions.answer: AI choices plus editable style, energy, duration, pins and section constraints
questions.selected_option: AI choices plus editable style, energy, duration, pins and section constraints
questions.interpretation: Expose AI-selected defaults and user editing for style, energy presets/custom curve, opener/closer and next-track pins, duration/range, tempo limits, section/cue boundaries and transition intensity. Changes validate feasibility and invalidate only affected future plans. Preserve active transitions and flag impossible duration/all-song combinations.

questions.question: How should the local desktop app launch?
options: A Mac launcher starts the local service and opens its browser UI
Require a cloud website
Run the MIDI communicator inside a browser tab
questions.answer: A Mac launcher starts the local service and opens its browser UI
questions.selected_option: A Mac launcher starts the local service and opens its browser UI
questions.interpretation: Deliver a local Mac launcher and TypeScript/HTML browser UI with a separate persistent Node service. Closing the tab does not kill performance. Bind to loopback, validate origin/session credentials and avoid exposing control APIs on the LAN. Desktop packaging must be tested on a clean local setup; an Electron wrapper is not required for this build.

questions.question: What responsiveness targets should we test first?
options: Measured budgets for controls, takeover and UI under load
Assume MIDI is instant
Promise sample-accurate JavaScript timers
questions.answer: Measured budgets for controls, takeover and UI under load
questions.selected_option: Measured budgets for controls, takeover and UI under load
questions.interpretation: Propose command-send to host-observation p95 <=30 ms and p99 <=75 ms; recognized human-input to AI cancellation p95 <=20 ms, p99 <=50 ms; observed state to app UI p95 <=100 ms. Report native Mixxx UI and audible onset separately, plus clock uncertainty, worst case and misses. No hard-real-time guarantee. Freeze a musically relevant host-quantized scheduling gate and measured onset budget in F01/M19 before claiming beat-critical support; failing budgets trigger focused optimization/native-scheduler work.

questions.question: What should validate musical quality?
options: Technical checks plus human listening against a baseline
Only successful MIDI sends
Let AI grade itself
questions.answer: Technical checks plus human listening against a baseline
questions.selected_option: Technical checks plus human listening against a baseline
questions.interpretation: Use repeatable Mixxx AutoDJ baseline and level-matched blind excerpts where feasible, covering open format, tempo/key differences, duplicate sections and manual interventions. Propose human ratings >=4/5 for naturalness and enjoyment on representative accepted sets, with no severe unintentional clashes, gaps or clipping. Keep subjective results and technical failures visible; human feedback is required before a runtime release.

questions.question: What happens when analysis, recording or UI is overloaded?
options: Protect MIDI/audio, reduce optional work and show degradation
Queue unlimited work
Hide gaps to keep the display smooth
questions.answer: Protect MIDI/audio, reduce optional work and show degradation
questions.selected_option: Protect MIDI/audio, reduce optional work and show degradation
questions.interpretation: Prioritize cancellation/releases and host state over telemetry, analysis, export and rendering. Bounded queues, process isolation and backpressure apply. Pause optional analysis/audio capture and downsample visual rendering before losing control responsiveness. Record gaps honestly; stale essential feedback disarms. Never drop already captured raw events silently while reporting lossless history.

questions.question: What should count as completion of this phase?
options: Complete reviewed planning docs and bounded tasks, committed to our fork
Claim the DJ is already working
Begin runtime implementation now
questions.answer: Complete reviewed planning docs and bounded tasks, committed to our fork
questions.selected_option: Complete reviewed planning docs and bounded tasks, committed to our fork
questions.interpretation: Complete discovery with explicitly delegated defaults, aligned goals/specs, an updated HTML direction page, bounded worker cards and traceability/validation, then commit/push planning artifacts to the existing fork. Runtime implementation starts only on a later user instruction. Unverified device/tool/performance facts remain future evidence requirements, not silently answered facts.

generation_end: End of autonomously AI-generated questionnaire record.
interaction_format: Discovery completed under user delegation; no further questionnaire answers required for this planning phase.

standing_preferences.answer: If the question has an asnwer that is both AI choseable and user defined alwasy pick that
standing_preferences.interpretation: When a question explicitly offers both automatic AI choice and user configuration/override, select that option without asking again. Continue asking distinct tradeoffs that are not resolved by this preference.

additional_requirements.user_text: Also utlize the cue points that controllers and softwares already use and are defined with midi
additional_requirements.requirement: Use existing Mixxx cue points, hotcues and applicable intro/outro markers as planning inputs and trigger supported operations via MIDI mappings. Preserve existing user markers; MIDI trigger availability and access to stored marker positions/labels require separate verification.

delegation.instruction: answer all the other questions your self
delegation.meaning: Assistant resolves remaining product choices as editable defaults; not individually user-confirmed answers. Existing explicit user answers take priority. No runtime implementation authorized.
